response.summary: 1 accept. F1: the PR #43 fix used df.where(...), which also blanked timestamp, so target-hour lookup could still fail. The 10.6 note now gives an as_of() helper. It keeps timestamp and available_at and blanks only the measurement columns of late rows. A 24-h lag example states what to check: the target-hour lookup succeeds, values that had arrived are kept, the rest are missing. Owner should check: pandas isn't installed here, so the new sketch was checked by reading, not run. pytest: 29 passed.

responses.reason: Correct. df.where(df.available_at <= issue_time) masks every column, including timestamp. A feature built with set_index('timestamp') then gets NaT labels for late rows, and .loc[target_hours] fails. The note now treats timestamp as a fixed grid of target hours. A new as_of() blanks only the measurement columns (everything except timestamp and available_at) of late rows. A shift(24) example states the expected result: lookup succeeds, values that had arrived are kept, the rest are missing.
